entities.summary:
Titus Flavius Sabinus was a Roman politician and soldier who played a crucial role in shaping the Roman Empire's early years. He was the elder son of Titus Flavius Sabinus and Vespasia Polla, and brother of the Emperor Vespasian.

Born in Reate, a small town in southern Italy, Titus Flavius Sabinus was groomed for greatness from an early age. His family's connections to the Roman elite and his own military prowess made him a prime candidate for a career in politics.

In 69 CE, Titus Flavius Sabinus was instrumental in the reign of Emperor Vespasian, who would go on to rule Rome for the next 10 years. However, his own rise to power was cut short when he was executed on orders from his brother, who had seized the throne for himself.

Titus Flavius Sabinus' legacy extends beyond his own time, however. His family's influence on Roman politics and society can still be seen today, with many of his descendants going on to play important roles in the empire's history.

The Roman historian Tacitus once described Titus Flavius Sabinus as 'a man of great ambition and a most excellent soldier'. This assessment captures the essence of his character and career, and serves as a reminder of the enduring impact of his life and work.
